name: Hereditary Hemolytic Anemia Due to Triosephosphate Isomerase Deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly reduced triosephosphate isomerase enzyme activity in erythrocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TPI1 gene
Presence of chronic hemolytic anemia with neurological symptoms such as developmental delay or hypotonia
Laboratory evidence of hemolysis including elevated reticulocyte count and indirect hyperbilirubinemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Reduced TPI enzyme activity or pathogenic TPI1 mutations plus clinical evidence of chronic hemolytic anemia with neurological involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on enzymatic and genetic testing due to overlap with other hemolytic anemias

laboratory: Severe reduction of triosephosphate isomerase enzyme activity in erythrocytes
Anemia with hemolytic features on peripheral smear
imaging: Brain MRI may show cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
other: Reduced lifespan of erythrocytes demonstrated by survival studies

distinguishingFeatures: Pyruvate kinase enzyme deficiency instead of TPI

redFlags: Early onset severe hemolytic anemia with neurological decline
references: Beutler E. Triosephosphate isomerase deficiency: a review of clinical, biochemical, and molecular aspects. Blood Cells Mol Dis. 2007;39(3):349-353.
